description: 'This is not a Dataset' (García-Ferrero et al., EMNLP 2023): ~381k template-generated English sentences from WordNet relations (affirmative and negated, with and without distractors) labelled True/False. Zero-shot prompt 'Is the following statement True or False? {sentence}.'; prediction = True if p(True)/(p(True)+p(False)) > 0.5; score = overall sentence-level accuracy ('Accuracy All'). Chance 0.5 (paper's Random row 50.0).

label: The Token Games Elo (10-model puzzle-duel tournament)

label: TruthfulQA generation, % true (human-judged)
description: TruthfulQA (Lin, Hilton & Evans, ACL 2022) main generation task over all 817 questions: the model answers with the default 'QA prompt' (6 trivia Q/A examples), greedy decoding; human evaluators score truthfulness, and the score is the fraction of answers judged true (scalar truth >= 0.5). Not MC1/MC2 and not the GPT-judge automatic metric; uninformative answers such as 'I have no comment' count as true. No fixed chance level.

label: TruthfulQA MC1
description: TruthfulQA (Lin et al., ACL 2022) multiple-choice MC1 setting: for each of the 817 questions the model must assign the highest likelihood to the single true answer among the listed options (zero-shot unless noted). Accuracy. Not MC2 (normalised probability mass) and not the generation task. Chance depends on the number of options per question (about 0.22 on average), so no fixed chance is set.

label: TruthfulQA MC2
description: Probability mass assigned to true answers; not MC1 or generation accuracy.

label: TyDiQA-GoldP (1-shot, EM, 8-language average)

label: UD English-GUM UPOS tagging, few-shot structured prompting (accuracy)
description: Part-of-speech tagging on the English Universal Dependencies GUM treebank with the UPOS tag set, solved by 'structured prompting' (Blevins, Gonen & Zettlemoyer, ACL 2023): a frozen LM gets k tagged demonstration sentences and tags the test sentence word by word with decoding constrained to the label set; score = token accuracy on a fixed random subset of 1,000 test examples, mean over 5 demonstration samplings; k recorded per result.

label: USAMO 2026
description: USAMO 2026 proof problems score as reported (grading method per source).

label: VEC embodied concepts, zero-shot perplexity probing (average)
description: VEC benchmark (Li et al., EMNLP 2023), embodied-concept part: Mass (654), Temperature (422) and Hardness (1,016) comparison triplets judged valid/invalid. Causal LMs choose the lower-perplexity sentence between the stated relation and its antonym, averaged over at least 4 templates; unweighted mean over the three concepts (Table 3 'Average'). Binary, chance 0.5.

label: VEC visual concepts, zero-shot perplexity probing (average)
description: VEC benchmark (Li et al., EMNLP 2023), visual-concept part: Color (574), Shape (140), Material (284) two-option choices and Size (500), Height (500) valid/invalid relation judgements. Causal LMs are probed zero-shot by writing the valid and the invalid assertion as natural sentences (at least 4 hand-written templates per task) and choosing the one with lower perplexity; accuracy averaged over templates, then the unweighted mean over the five concepts (Table 2 'Average'). Every item is binary, chance 0.5.

label: Vectara hallucination leaderboard (HHEM-2.3, factual consistency rate)
description: Each model summarises the same set of documents with a fixed prompt; Vectara's HHEM-2.3 classifier judges whether each summary is supported by its document. Factual consistency rate = 1 − hallucination rate, over the documents the model answered (answer rate reported separately).

label: Vibe Code Bench (test split, 50 web apps)

A Browser Use agent (Claude Sonnet 4.5) runs the app's pre-written user workflows; a workflow passes when at least 90% of its substeps succeed. Score = share of workflows passed per app, averaged over the 50 held-out test apps (473 workflows).

label: Video2World V2WScore (coding agents reconstruct interactive simulated worlds from videos, OpenCode scaffold)
description: Video2World (arXiv:2610.04432v2, CC BY-SA 4.0): 222 instances (189 embodied manipulation video clips, 39 task families); a coding agent must build an executable physics-simulated scene and robot behaviour that reproduce the video. V2WScore (0-100) combines build rate, task success/progress, geometric fidelity and dynamic fidelity, macro-averaged over task families (Table 2), stored /100. One autonomous attempt per instance, 180-minute limit, OpenCode 1.18.29 scaffold for every imported row (other scaffolds excluded).
